- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.28) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–4% to align with true decline.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or oscillating), model often fails to correct downward; apply a 2–5% downward bias if price has been above 30-day moving average for >7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate true volatility in sentiment-driven periods; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment variance >0.20 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling (e.g., +0.11 sentiment, -0.5% price), model often misreads sentiment; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment-weighted mean, not pure trend.
